title: Convo Wavefront Assembler — KV-squeeze batch formation for low-jitter streaming
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: For streaming chat completions we need a batch formation strategy that minimizes end-to-end jitter for low-latency responses while maximizing KV cache reuse and keeping per-GPU memory pressure predictable. Current slab-based microbatching (see ENG-52345/ENG-45267) either prioritizes throughput (large batches) or latency (immediate flush) but does poorly when sessions have highly variable turn lengths and when KV segments fragment GPU memory.

Proposal: Implement the 'Convo Wavefront Assembler' heuristic: a wavefront groups in-flight streaming turns across conversations by their relative progress through the model (current sequence length fraction) and by prefix KV reuse score. The assembler emits microbatches when either (1) a wavefront density threshold is reached, (2) the oldest request in a wavefront reaches a hard latency deadline, or (3) downstream GPU memory headroom falls below a safety margin and we need to enforce compaction. The key innovation is KV-squeeze: before forming a microbatch, we attempt to co-locate turns whose KV segments overlap or whose prefix token hashes collide in the cache region to allow zero-copy KV sharing and avoid duplicative KV allocations.

Design goals: reduce tail latency (p95/p99), reduce duplicate KV memory usage per-GPU, maintain stable token throughput, and allow graceful degradation under memory pressure. Heuristic should be tunable by per-customer routing policy (latency-first vs cost-first) and support canary toggling per-dedicated pool.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for streaming first-token improves or remains within 5% of baseline for latency-first customers
GPU KV duplicate memory usage decreased by >=20% in benchmarked chat workload (mixed-turn lengths)
No regression in aggregate tokens/sec beyond 10% for throughput-first configs
Metric dashboards for wavefront hit-rate, KV-squeeze reuse rate, microbatch size distribution, and memory headroom are instrumented and visible in Console
Rollout plan with canary on 1 dedicated pool and automatic rollback if stall-rate > 0.5% within 1 hour
updates: 2026-02-18 - Marco Chen: Created ticket. Initial problem write-up and high-level proposal. Noted overlap with prior batching tickets but this approach focuses on cross-conversation KV co-location rather than time-window bundling.
2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Added quantitative goals and suggested safety margins for GPU headroom. Requested metrics to track (wavefront_density, kv_squeeze_rate, microbatch_latency_spread).

2026-02-25 - Marco Chen: Prototype completed — wavefront coordinator in front of slab allocator. Local microbench (simulated 100k sessions, mixed-turn lengths) shows 26% drop in duplicate KV allocations and 6% p95 improvement for latency-first profile. Attached benchmark logs to design doc.

2026-03-01 - Elena Rodriguez (Perf): Reviewed prototype. Identified two trade-offs: (1) hash-based KV grouping reduces duplicates but increases decision CPU cycles per-request; (2) aggressive co-location can increase p50 latency for short-turn interactive queries. Proposed adaptive CPU budget limiter for assembler to avoid CPU becoming a new bottleneck.

2026-03-04 - Aisha Patel: Started integration tests on staging dedicated pool (dp-staging-3). Observed drop in GPU memory headroom under synthetic spike tests; tuned compaction-trigger from 120MB to 180MB safety margin which stabilized stalls. Recorded experiment links in PR.

2026-03-06 - Marco Chen: Updated heuristics: add 'age-weight' to wavefront scoring so long-waiting requests are promoted, and introduce soft-deadline flush where wavefront emits for small batches if request age > 120ms. Preparing canary plan; ETA to deploy 2026-03-12 to one dedicated pool.
Open questions: desired default soft-deadline across customer tiers, acceptable CPU overhead cap (suggest 2% of request CPU budget), and whether to expose a knob in Console for KV-squeeze aggressive mode.
